title: Rational sections with support preserve finite-constant-model bounded constructibility
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$; all schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in it. Let $\Lambda=E$, with the condensed ring $S\mapsto C(S,E)$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], or $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with the condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] whose sections on a profinite set $S$ are the continuous maps $S\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with image in some finite subextension; pull it back to $\Lambda_T$ on the small pro-étale site of each scheme $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For such $T$ let $\Dbc(T,\Lambda)\subset D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ be the full subcategory of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: bounded complexes of $\Lambda_T$-modules each of whose cohomology sheaves admits a finite stratification of $T$ by constructible locally closed subschemes on each of which it has a finite constant local model (pro-étale locally of the form $\Lambda\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$ with $P$ a finitely presented $\Lambda(*)$-module).

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of such schemes, and let $R\underline\Gamma_Z:D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ be the derived functor of sections with support in $Z$ of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support]. Then for every $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ one has $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$.

source.place: last clause '$R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(Z,\Lambda)$', with $\Dbc$ read in the finite-constant-local-model convention of sk-def-sfb-constructible used by sk-prop-sf-existence and sk-thm-restriction (the existing DAG node det-prop-closed-adjoint-constructible-support states it for the convention of sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible)

proof.text: Finite type over Spec k gives locally Noetherian X and Z; quasi-compact structure maps give compact X and Z. The open immersion j is quasi-compact over locally Noetherian X. Its source U is locally Noetherian and compact. All three schemes are therefore quasi-separated. Give U the composite structure map j followed by the structure map of X; finite type and separatedness follow by composition.

For each of the two coefficient choices use [lem-sfb-pullback-constant-model-constructible] to preserve constructible cohomology under i and j. Compare the ordinary upperStar, which uses extension of scalars, with formalSupportPullback, which restricts along the inverse coefficient isomorphism, using Mod.extendScalarsIsoComapInv. Transport the finite-cover witnesses along this isomorphism. The exact-functor boundedness and homology comparison show that the formal derived pullbacks preserve bounded constant-model constructibility.

Use the existing formal_closed_support_adjunction realization of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction], at the actual derived-category Hom universe, to obtain its distinguished localization triangle and fiber isomorphism for F=i_*RGamma_Z K. No coefficient or constructibility assumptions enter this formal input.

Apply [lem-sfb-rational-open-direct-image-constructible] to j and the constructible formal derived pullback j^*K from step 2. The source of that declaration is ordinary upperStar, but its direct-image functor is exactly lowerStar used by the formal triangle. Rewrite ringChar k=p to satisfy its standing characteristic hypotheses.

Install the isomorphism and triangulated-closure instances on X and isomorphism closure on Z from [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated]. Apply ext_of_isTriangulatedClosed₁ to the distinguished triangle and its constructible second and third vertices. This proves that F is bounded constant-model constructible.

Apply derived formal pullback along i to F, using step 2. Transport the resulting membership along the inverse of the formal fiber isomorphism RGamma_Z K ≅ i^*F. Carry out the argument once for each finite intermediate field E and once for the algebraic-closure coefficient. For the latter, choose the bottom finite intermediate field only as the unused E argument of the already stated two-clause open-image theorem.
